thread:
Ella: Hey team, customer (org: acme-ml) reporting 404s + 400s after upgrading to @redwood/sdk-js v0.27. They say chat.create is missing and some auth param names changed. Can we triage?
Matt: Oof, which endpoint exactly? Chat.create vs chat.create_session or similar?
Ella: Root message from customer: 'after npm i @redwood/sdk@0.27 our app started getting 404 for /v1/chat.create and 400s for auth header'. They provided a small repro and Node logs.
Sophie: Likely a breaking rename. v0.27 had the route name normalization change iirc. Does the SDK now call /v1/chat/create or /v1/chat.create?
Matt: I pulled the SDK diff — the client uses route keys now (dot notation) but the backend routing uses dashed endpoints for older API versions. If a customer pins API version unspecified, it can mismatch.
Ella: Customer says they didn't set apiVersion explicitly; they rely on default. They updated SDK only.
support-bot: (automated) Please include: SDK version, Node version, sample request, and full response body.
Ella: Customer attached logs. Key bits: 
```
Request: POST /v1/chat.create
Headers: authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX
Body: { model: "redwood-alpha", messages: [...] }
Response: 404 {"error":"route_not_found","route":"/v1/chat.create"}
```
And another case: 400 with body: `{ "error": "unknown_param", "param": "sessionToken" }`
Sophie: Aha — sessionToken vs session_token vs session-token. We recently added optional sessionToken support in SDK for multiplexing, but server expects session_token query param for legacy routes. That mismatch will produce unknown_param or drop auth which triggers 400.
Matt: Also saw a note: retries in the SDK will re-send requests without idempotency key by default if not configured. Customer got charged excessive tokens during retry storms. They ran into a loop with 429->retry->400 and kept consuming tokens.
Ella: Customer wants a mitigation now. Suggestions?
Sophie: Short term: ask them to pin @redwood/sdk-js@0.26 in package.json and redeploy. That should restore previous wire format. Also recommend setting REDWOOD_API_VERSION explicitly to the server version, e.g. process.env.REDWOOD_API_VERSION = "2025-01-01".
Matt: Also advise enabling the debug env to gather network traces: `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 node app.js` and capture request/response pairs. Ask for sample cURL too.
Ella: I prepared a short repro we can send: 
```
// Node repro snippet
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-alpha', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }], sessionToken: 'abc' });
```
This returns 400 unknown_param sessionToken on v0.27 in their env.
support-bot: (automated) Escalation created: SEV-LOW ticket #SEV-2381 assigned to eng-runtime.
eng-runtime-oncall: Looping in eng-runtime. Can you attach the raw request/response headers and the Node stack trace? Also include package.json and lockfile. We'll check route mapping table and the compatibility shim.
Sophie: I've looked at internal diff: in v0.27 we introduced `routeKey` translation and a new param name `sessionToken` in SDK surfaces, but the compatibility shim wasn't enabled for some legacy hosted tenants. If the control plane didn't flip the flag for the tenant, they'll hit mismatched server handlers.
Ella: Next steps for support to ask customer: 1) package.json + yarn.lock or package-lock.json 2) output of `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` run 3) confirm if they can temporarily pin to 0.26 (we'll provide exact command) 4) org id and workspace id so eng-runtime can check tenant flags.
Matt: Workaround command: `npm i @redwood/sdk@0.26 --save-exact` then restart. Also advise setting `REDWOOD_RETRY_STRATEGY=exponential` and `REDWOOD_MAX_RETRIES=1` to avoid billing loops until fixed.
Sophie: I'll open internal issue and note affected route `/v1/chat.create` + param mapping. Reference: https://redwood.internal/issues/REND-2319 (internal).
eng-runtime-oncall: If customer can provide org id, we can toggle the backward-compat shim for them temporarily while we release a server-side fix.
Ella: I messaged the customer asking for the artifacts. They've replied with package.json and said they can pin to 0.26 for now. They've asked for ETA on permanent fix.
Matt: ETA depends on rollout; I'll coordinate with runtime and release tomorrow morning. For now confirm pin + retry env changes.
Sophie: Add note to the ticket: highlight billing exposure — ask billing team to review if excessive token usage occurred during the retry window.
Ella: Thanks — marking this thread resolved for support. I'll update ticket #SEV-2381 when eng-runtime confirms shim toggle. :thumbsup:
